title: Generating MNIST Digits with Flow Matching
summary: A generative model that learns to turn random noise into handwritten digits.
description: I first tested flow matching on eight clusters of points in two dimensions to see how the model moved noise toward the target distribution. I then adapted the course-provided U-Net to generate MNIST digits and compared Euler and Heun sampling at different step counts.

For the final model, I chose 50-step Heun sampling to balance recognition and runtime. On 2,000 unfiltered samples, the course classifier assigned a digit with more than 99% confidence to 90.9% of the images. Its predictions covered all ten digits.

images.alt: Grid of 50 generated white handwritten digits on black tiles, including a few ambiguous shapes.

title: Panorama Stitching from Overlapping Photos
summary: Two overlapping photos of an atrium, aligned and stitched into one wider view.
description: I used OpenCV’s SIFT features to find matching points, then used RANSAC to reject unreliable matches and estimate the perspective transform. I implemented inverse warping to align the images on a shared canvas and used feather blending to soften the seam.

I tested the pipeline on photos taken by rotating the camera and on a flat wall photographed from two positions. I also tried moving the camera sideways through a scene with objects at different depths. In that case, a single transform couldn’t align the foreground and background at the same time.

title: Text-to-Image Search with CLIP
summary: A search interface that finds photos in a small collection from a written description.
description: I used pretrained CLIP to encode a collection of 20 photos and rank them by cosine similarity to a text query. I cached the photo embeddings so each search only had to encode the query and score the existing vectors.

I built a Gradio interface that lets users enter a description and choose how many ranked results to see. I also compared query phrasings and examined close matches, like the apple slices ranked third for the banana query.

title: Multi-Dialect Vietnamese Text to Speech
description: Fine-tuned and evaluated a multi-dialect Vietnamese TTS system using F5-TTS on ~71 hours of dialect-annotated speech across Northern, Central, and Southern Vietnamese.
Designed evaluation workflow using WER, MOS, and qualitative error analysis to measure speech intelligibility, naturalness, and dialect preservation across training checkpoints.
Built and presented an interactive Gradio demo for dialect-controlled Vietnamese speech synthesis with generated audio playback and mel spectrogram visualization.
summary: A Vietnamese speech synthesis system with selectable Northern, Central, and Southern dialects.

title: Distributed Auction Marketplace System
description: Built a container based distributed auction marketplace using Docker Compose, with a centralized controller, stateless service nodes, and replicated SQLite backed storage nodes.
Implemented primary-backup replication with controller managed health checks and automatic primary failover to maintain availability during storage node failures.
Designed autoscaling for the service node layer using rolling request rate monitoring and round robin routing to scale request handling under burst traffic.
summary: A distributed auction marketplace with replicated storage, automatic failover, and autoscaling to handle node failures and changing demand.

title: Neural Network Compression for Ventricular Arrhythmia Detection
description: Optimized a deep learning model for cardiac arrhythmia detection tailored for resource constrained microcontrollers.
Compressed model size by implementing Depthwise Separable Convolutions, BatchNorm folding, and Quantization Aware Training (QAT).
Evaluated tradeoffs across INT8, INT4, and INT2 bit widths to identify the viable precision for accurate classification.
summary: Exploring how network redesign and quantization can shrink an arrhythmia detection model for resource-constrained microcontrollers.

title: DaeTrace
description: Architected and built a full-stack productivity tracking system using a Chrome Extension (Manifest V3) and Firebase for MinneHack 2026.
Designed scalable data models for user activity, session metadata, and domain categorization.
Implemented session state management and dynamic domain-blocking logic, leveraging Firestore real-time listeners to synchronize data consistently between the extension and web dashboard.
summary: A browser extension and web dashboard for tracking browsing activity and managing distractions through domain blocking.

title: Gamblr
description: Developed a full-stack web application for tracking gambling habits with real time data synchronization using Firestore NoSQL database.
Built a fully customizable drag and drop dashboard allowing users to personalize their workspace with interactive widgets for data visualization and spending analysis.
Implemented voice transcription for visit notes using Google Cloud Speech to Text API integrated with Firebase Functions and created a practice mode featuring a Three.js 3D slot machine simulation.
summary: A customizable dashboard for tracking gambling habits, reviewing spending, and recording visit notes.

title: Nap Finder
description: Engineered a CRUD API for locations, reviews, and users, featuring data aggregation for average ratings.
Implemented an interactive map view with dynamic pins that navigate users to pre-filtered detail pages for specific nap spot locations.
Developed comprehensive spot detail pages displaying dynamic building information, user reviews, and specific access requirements.

title: Pokémon Type Classifier
description: Developed image classification models to predict Pokémon types using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs) on a custom labeled dataset of Pokémon images.
Preprocessed and augmented over 1,000 images to improve model robustness and handle class imbalance.
Evaluated model performance using precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrices; refined hyperparameters to boost accuracy.

title: Visual Transit Simulator
description: Contributed to the design, documentation, and implementation of a Visual Transit Simulator modeling vehicle and passenger behavior across routes.
Created UML class diagrams and Javadoc documentation while adhering to Google Java style guidelines.
Designed and executed unit tests to ensure robustness and compliance with project requirements.

title: SQLite Clone
description: Developed a lightweight relational database inspired by SQLite, implementing core database functionalities in C.
Utilized a B-tree index structure to optimize query performance and minimize full table scans.
Engineered a custom storage format for data persistence, managing in-memory structures and disk I/O operations.

title: Simple Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) System
description: Built a lightweight RAG pipeline integrating Ollama models for embedding and generation.
Implemented text chunk embedding, vector database storage, and cosine similarity search for context retrieval.
Combined retrieved context with a language model prompt to generate grounded responses.

title: Multi-Threaded HTTP Server
description: Built an multi-threaded HTTP web server in C that handles multiple clients using a thread pool.
Implemented TCP socket setup, request parsing, and response generation for file retrieval.
Created a thread-safe queue for managing client connections and ensured clean server shutdown.

title: Simple Working Implementation Shell (Swish)
description: Developed a simplified Unix shell supporting command execution, directory management, and I/O redirection.
Implemented process creation, signal handling, and job control using system calls like fork(), exec(), waitpid(), and sigaction().
Extended functionality to handle pipelines, enabling commands to communicate via pipes for parallel execution.

title: Minitar
description: Created a simplified Posix-compliant version of the tar utility using C and the stdio library.
Implemented archive creation, extraction, listing, and updating with proper 512-byte block formatting.
Handled file I/O, header metadata generation, and error checking for reliable archive operations.
